cells.tense: You are holding several true things at once right now without forcing them to agree yet.
cells.ask: Write one true thing in a sentence of your own and leave it where you'll see it tomorrow, not to decide anything, just to have it outside your head.
cells.core:
Several true things are in your hands at once, and you can carry them without making them agree. Nothing has had to become a position. You say what you've noticed and you stay reachable while you say it, which is rarer than it sounds.

What this balance can feed next is a little structure: one of the true things given a shape, a sentence on paper, a line you keep where you'll see it again. Writing one of them down doesn't close the others. It gives what you see somewhere to land besides the conversation you happen to be in. Pick one and write it plainly, as yours, and let that be enough for today.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a choice you have not made and treating each option as though it were already wrong.
cells.ask: Take one of the things you're holding, commit to it for this week only, and leave the rest alone until the week is up.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of where you are. Every truth that comes in gets checked against a future where it already failed, so you keep gathering and keep bracing instead of letting one thing do for now. The many truths aren't the problem; the forward lean is.

What settles this is a direction chosen out of the many, not instead of them: one light for now, the others still in view. Choose one, hold it for the week, and stop re-deciding against the ones you set aside. What you perceive lands cleanly when you're not standing a month ahead of it. You don't have to know the ending to walk the week.

cells.tense: You have stopped saying what you see, and the room has gone quieter than what you hold.
cells.ask: Say one true thing out loud today, small and in plain words, and let the answer or the silence come without going back over it.
cells.core:
You see what's true and you don't say it. Not from confusion — plenty arrives, and it stays where it lands, unoffered. Other people in the room are working with less than you have, and they don't know it, and you keep letting that be the arrangement.

What pulls you back is contact at the level of the missing piece, not more seeing. One sentence said out loud to someone, small, and then whatever comes next comes. Don't push harder at the perceiving; it isn't dry. Say one thing and let it be heard or not, and let that be the whole of the job for today. You don't have to be sure of it first.

cells.tense: You are already telling true from false in the room and talking about it as though the room were doing it.
cells.ask: Name one call you made recently as yours, plainly, out loud where the people it touches can hear you say it.
cells.core:
The telling apart is running well. You notice what holds and what doesn't, and which one is worth keeping, and it shapes what you do next without much argument. That's the thing working — reads that land, other people steadying on them, the sense in the room that somebody's actually tracking it.

What's absent is the claim. You speak as if the read were something the room handed you, while the room fills with your take on it. The plainest form of this is the one you already run: a private sense of what's right, nothing announced. Name one call as yours, once, where it counts, and let them hear who made it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a reader can recognise a specific room, teacher, or reading failure in their past because there are too many truths held now — the record does not link the state to any event, so the Too Little cell must name only the door and the quiet knowing, not what happened behind it. A reader could reasonably say they never stopped perceiving, only stopped trusting the perception, and the ask still holds because it names nothing about the cause. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'the light is there and the sorting isn't' — it sounds complete but tells the person nothing they can use, so it is replaced with what is held and what is not yet chosen.
